answer: To resist Sybil swarms, nodes deploy cryptographic attestation chains paired with zero-knowledge proofs to verify identity legitimacy across the network horizon. Rather than harbor redundant clones, the protocol imposes an exponential capital exhaustion bonding curve: creating nth agents demands 2^n stake. A rogue swarm cannot root like a sturdy juniper; superlinear attacker cost rapidly bleeds adversary reserves, guaranteeing economic security.
